Replaced redundant 'Questions Before Enrolling' section with the affiliate-fit note.

File 13 (AC short cycling): Added 8-row causes table with diagnostic tells, fix cost ranges ($5–$8,000), and time-to-diagnose (2 min–60 min). Added 'Call a Tech vs DIY' decision table. Added 'When to Act Immediately' criteria. Added 'Questions to Ask Your Technician'. EPA WaterSense statistics page (https://www.epa.gov/watersense/statistics-and-facts) confirmed 82 gal/person/day total, 70% indoor; USGS figure used for per-capita range.

risks: Budget billing mechanics (file 16) describe a standard 12-month average calculation common to most US utilities, but some utilities use adjusted projections or 6-month averages. The article advises readers to verify their specific utility's terms in writing, which mitigates this risk.
AC fix cost ranges (file 13) are national estimates and may vary significantly by region. All ranges are labeled as estimates with explicit caveats.

Water usage table (file 06) uses EPA/USGS data blended with per-person estimates; the per-capita 58-82 gpcd range is a composite and may not match every household. The table is labeled with the range and a note about variation.
unknowns: Whether the specific budget billing calculation formulas used by some utilities (e.g., those using projected future usage vs. past 12 months) differ materially from the standard model described. Article mitigates by advising readers to verify their utility's written terms.
